title: Tenant quarantine + snapshot-driven embedding onboarding playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: New embedding variants keep regressing semantic quality for a small subset of tenants while improving aggregate metrics. We need a reproducible onboarding + versioning approach that isolates risky cohorts, measures semantic drift with snapshot-based checkpoints, and ties rollout decisions to both quality and latency budgets. Goal: create an operational playbook and runtime controls for per-tenant quarantine, snapshot evals, staged traffic promotion, and automated rollback triggers. Deliverables: 1) onboarding playbook doc with staged gating; 2) runtime flags/aliasing for tenant quarantine and soft-alias fallbacks; 3) telemetry dashboards and automated regression detectors; 4) small infra to persist per-cohort snapshots and semver-tagged embeddings for drift comparison.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding playbook published in Confluence with step-by-step gated phases: sample, snapshot, quarantine, staged-vote, promote/sunset
Runtime feature toggles implemented: tenant_quarantine, snapshot_alias, soft_alias_fallback
Telemetry: per-tenant semantic similarity drift metric and latency-percentile chart available in Console for any rollout
Automated rollback rule: if cohort semantic delta > 0.06 average cosine drop OR 95th latency increases by >25% within first 48h, traffic is auto-routed back to previous alias
Smoke tests and e2e canary runbook completed and linked to PRs
Docs list required commitments for Dedicated/Private customers (e.g., snapshot retention, storage cost estimate)
